S067.name: Preoccupation_with_Appearance
S067.description: Preoccupation with one or more perceived defects or flaws in physical appearance that are not observable or appear slight to others.

subtypes.Skin Defects: Excessive preoccupation with practically invisible acne, scars, or complexion.
subtypes.Facial Features: Preoccupation with the shape or size of the nose, eyes, or mouth, which appear normal to others.
subtypes.Asymmetry: Excessive obsession with the face or body not being perfectly symmetrical.
subtypes.Muscle Dysmorphia: The belief that one's body is too small or insufficiently muscular despite being normal or muscular.
subtypes.Specific Body Parts: Obsession that specific parts like hair, teeth, or chest are ugly or abnormal.

S068.name: Appearance_Related_Repetitive_Behaviors
S068.description: Repetitive behaviors or mental acts performed in response to appearance concerns.

subtypes.Mirror Checking or Avoidance: Compulsively checking oneself in the mirror frequently or, conversely, avoiding mirrors strictly.
subtypes.Excessive Camouflaging: Spending excessive time and effort to hide perceived flaws using makeup, clothes, hats, or sunglasses.
subtypes.Skin Picking: Picking or manipulating the skin excessively to remove or 'fix' flaws.
subtypes.Reassurance Seeking: Repetitively asking others for confirmation that one's appearance is okay or not strange.
subtypes.Comparing: Constantly comparing one's body parts with those of passersby or celebrities.
subtypes.Seeking Cosmetic Procedures: Repeatedly seeking or receiving plastic surgery or dermatological procedures.

symptom.disease_info: Body Dysmorphic Disorder (BDD) is characterized by a persistent preoccupation with one or more perceived defects or flaws in physical appearance that are not observable or appear slight to others, accompanied by repetitive behaviors or mental acts related to these concerns. The preoccupation causes clinically significant distress or impairment in social, occupational, or other important areas of functioning and is not better explained by concerns about body fat or weight in an eating disorder. Onset is typically in adolescence, but it can emerge or worsen later in life, often triggered by developmental changes, social comparison, or stressful life events. BDD is distinguished from normal appearance concerns by its intensity, the degree of functional impairment, and the often poor or absent insight into the unreasonableness of the beliefs, and it overlaps phenomenologically with obsessive–compulsive and related disorders.

patient.personality: Thang is a disciplined, routine‑oriented man who takes quiet pride in methodical work, careful planning, and steady, practical living.
patient.stressor: In his early fifties, Thang was told at a routine check‑up that he had elevated blood pressure and cholesterol, which frightened him because of family stories about sudden strokes and heart attacks. Already someone who monitored his garden and finances closely, he began monitoring his body just as carefully, initially in a reasonable effort to improve his health through diet and exercise. Over time, a comment from a coworker about him "looking older" and his own observations of changes in his skin and midsection seemed to confirm a fear that his body was failing him, and he increasingly focused on what he saw as visible evidence of deterioration rather than lab numbers or stamina. This preoccupation started to dominate his mornings and evenings, cutting into sleep, family meals, and his enjoyment of gardening and woodworking, and when his wife complained that he was constantly checking and criticizing his appearance and avoiding social gatherings with extended family out of embarrassment, she urged him to seek professional help; he finally agreed after noticing that these concerns were affecting his concentration and reliability at work.
patient.chief_complaint: “I spend way too much time checking how I look because I’m convinced something is wrong with my body, and it’s starting to interfere with my work and family life.”

S067.name: Preoccupation_with_Appearance
S067.description: Preoccupation with one or more perceived defects or flaws in physical appearance that are not observable or appear slight to others.
S067.manifestation: Lately, whenever I catch sight of myself—especially my face and this loose skin and thick waist—I can’t stop thinking how worn-out and sick I look, like my body is falling apart in front of everyone, even when my wife and kids tell me I look fine for my age, and that thought just runs in my head all day while I’m out mowing or trimming hedges.

S068.name: Appearance_Related_Repetitive_Behaviors
S068.description: Repetitive behaviors or mental acts performed in response to appearance concerns.
S068.manifestation: Every morning and night I end up standing in the bathroom and bedroom mirrors for long stretches, lifting my shirt, poking at the sagging around my stomach, pulling at the wrinkles and spots on my face, changing shirts three or four times, asking my wife over and over if I look older or bloated, and sometimes I just skip family gatherings because I can’t get past what I see in the mirror.
